---
title: Events and webhooks
description: How an app learns what changed in an instance, by reading the event stream or by receiving webhooks.
---

An app that shows someone's data needs to know when another app changes it. Marfa records each change to an item or an edge as an **event** in one log, in order. An event here is a record of a change, not a `core.event` item, which holds a calendar event.

There are two ways to follow the log: your app pulls events from the event stream, or Marfa pushes them to your service as webhooks.

<EventFlow />

## The event log

Each event is named by its **event type**, such as `item.created`, `edge.deleted` or `rows.changed`, sent once for each batch a [table](/build/tables) takes. Changes to items, their tags and extensions, their rows and edges add events, and Marfa adds `attention.raised`, for a credential holding `instance.read`, when it finds something new that needs the owner's attention. The Catalog's [Events](/catalog/events) page lists every event type, exactly when each is sent, and its fields.

**Other writes add none:** a change to a type, a key, a webhook or a setting, a blob upload, and a write that changes nothing. A refused write adds none either. An item event carries the item as it stands after the change.

Event IDs rise with every event, so the last ID an app handled, its **cursor**, says exactly where it stopped. The log keeps events for `event_log_retention_days`, 30 days by default.

A credential sees only the events about what it can read: an item event needs the item's type in its [type map](/build/access#what-a-credential-reaches), and an edge event the edge type and the item it points from.

## The event stream

The [event stream](/api-reference/event-stream/streamEvents) is a long-lived connection your app opens. Here the CLI follows it for bookmarks while another app saves one and tags it:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa events --type core.bookmark
```

```text
-  stream_cursor  30
-  stream_live  30
31  item.created  01a1f14d-c8b1-705b-b50e-f4d2b04bcccf
32  metadata.changed  01a1f14d-c8b1-705b-b50e-f4d2b04bcccf
```

</Terminal>

The stream starts by saying where the log stands. Send your cursor, and Marfa replays every event after it, sends `stream_live` when you've caught up, and then sends each new event as it happens. Resume from your cursor after a break, and you get every later event **exactly once**. A stream can name up to ten types, each with its subtypes, and leave out edge events with `edges=none`.

If you've been away longer than the log keeps events, the stream ends with `catchup_too_old`, and your app reads its data again from the start. [Keep a copy in sync](/build/keep-in-sync) shows how to follow the stream and handle each way it ends. The Swift SDK and a [device](/build/devices) follow it for you.

## Webhooks

A webhook works the other way round: Marfa posts each new event to your service. You register a URL and the event types you want, with a credential that holds `webhooks.manage`. A key or an app's grant holds at most 100 subscriptions.

Each delivery is signed in `X-Marfa-Signature`, so your service can check it came from your instance. A delivery your service fails, times out, or answers `408` or `429` is tried again, eight times in all over a little more than five hours. Any other `4xx` ends it at once. Its record then says `succeeded` or `failed`, and a failed one can be sent again.

**A webhook has no cursor and no replay:** it delivers only events written after you registered it. Deliveries can arrive **out of order**, so a receiver keeps the highest event ID it has applied for each item and ignores an older one. A bulk write reaches webhooks only when it asks to, with `enable_fanout: true`, and a webhook delivers only what its credential may read.

By default a webhook can only post to a public address, so the instance can't be turned against its own network. When receivers are on a private network, the owner allows them with the `allow_private_addresses` [setting](/run/settings), which takes a recent sign-in.

| Use | When |
| --- | --- |
| The event stream | An app needs every change, including what it missed while away |
| A webhook | A service reacts to changes as they happen, such as sending a message when a document is signed |

[Receive webhooks](/build/receive-webhooks) shows how to register one and check each delivery.

The rules behind this page are in the [events](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/events.md) and [reach](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/reach.md) chapters of the contract.
